section_summary: This section combines embassy transmittals of Japanese Home Department sanitary reports, internal filing notes, and cross-references concerning tuberculosis treatments, public-health institutions, and administrative changes. Its principal document is Richard F. Boyce’s extensive 1936 report on sanitary conditions in Japan, covering hospitals, medical personnel, tuberculosis, leprosy, infectious diseases, quarantine, mortality, and the Japan Red Cross Society. The section concludes with Treasury and State Department correspondence praising Boyce’s report and a 1937 reference to the establishment of Japan’s Ministry of Health and Social Affairs.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from despatch no. 607 on the Rockefeller Foundation gift
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, United States Embassy at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s acceptance of a Rockefeller Foundation donation to establish a public hygiene institute.
subfiles.summary: The Cabinet announced its acceptance of a large Rockefeller Foundation donation for a public hygienic institute. A Central Sanitary Bureau official described the cooperative government-foundation project as the basis for a systematic campaign against disease with importance throughout Japan and the Far East.

subfiles.title: Sanitary Conditions of Japan
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul at Yokohama
subfiles.about: Provides a broad statistical and institutional survey of medicine, sanitation, hospitals, disease control, quarantine, mortality, and Red Cross work in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Boyce compiled the report chiefly from the 1935 and 1936 Japan-Manchoukuo Year Books and a February 11, 1936 Japan Advertiser article, intending it as background material for the United States Public Health Service. It surveys medical practitioners, hospitals, asylums, tuberculosis and leprosy institutions, venereal- and infectious-disease facilities, vaccination, trachoma, patent medicines, laboratories, and quarantine. Extensive tables record hospital capacity, patient numbers, disease incidence, mortality, and life expectancy, while the tuberculosis sections emphasize the disease’s heavy toll and a proposed nationwide program of free clinics and sanatoria. The final portion describes the Japan Red Cross Society’s hospitals, disaster relief, overseas work, leadership, finances, and the 1934 International Red Cross Congress in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Treasury Department appreciation of Boyce’s sanitary report
subfiles.from: Josephine Roche, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Conveys the Public Health Service’s appreciation for Richard F. Boyce’s report on sanitary conditions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Treasury thanks Boyce for his March 2 sanitary report, of great interest to the Public Health Service, and asks for more on Japanese health conditions.

subfiles.title: State Department letter forwarding Treasury appreciation to Yokohama
subfiles.about: Forwards the Treasury Department’s thanks for the report Sanitary Conditions of Japan and informs the consul that it received a very-good rating.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Treasury's April 3 praise of Boyce's report to Yokohama and says the Department rated it VERY GOOD.
